correctness.rationale: For m=n+1, Legendre gives v_p(Q_n)=floor((m-1)/(p-1))-(m-s_p(m))/(p-1), nonnegative by divisibility by p-1 and s_p(m)>=1. In particular v_2(Q_n)=s_2(m)-1 and v_3(Q_n)=(s_3(m)-1)/2 for odd m, (s_3(m)-2)/2 for even m. Therefore any squarefree Q_n has binary digit sum <=2, i.e. m=2^a or 2^a+2^b with a>b>=0, 0<=a<=16384, m<=2^16384. The low 24 ternary digits are a lower bound for the full ternary digit sum, so the radix-3 residue sieve discards no possible squarefree m. Parity-specific complete ternary sums reduce all 134,225,920 two-one patterns plus single powers to exactly 42 index candidates (59 retained by preliminary filter). Complete exact sieve and Legendre valuations at every prime p<=n+1 for these 42 give precisely seven p^2 obstructions and 35 survivors. Independent NumPy-vectorized residue enumeration over ALL pairs, distinct from the supplied Python verifier, reproduced the full list in 1.763 seconds; independent brute force at every n<4096 gave the same survivors. The boundary n=0 (Q_0=1), n=2^16384-1, parity, empty product, and zero valuations for p>n+1 are respected. Finite certificate supports only n<2^16384; no global final-squarefree claim.

evidence: Senge--Straus (1973), as stated in OEIS A096288, proves s_2(m)+s_3(m)->infinity; combining that theorem with the p=2,3 Legendre valuation identities ALREADY implies there are only finitely many squarefree Q_n.
Stewart (1980) supplies effective lower estimates for mixed-base digit sums but the material inspected gives no explicit 2^16384 census or 35-index set.
Bedhouche--Farhi Proposition 3.2 supplies factorial divisibility; Theorem 3.4 controls valuations at large primes, but neither is a squarefree global census.

The claimed finite list is not a corollary of just the published qualitative theorem or source product identities without actual exhaustive computation.

value.rationale: A363596 is a named natural prime-product factorial quotient with an explicitly discussed unknown last-squarefree occurrence. Its exact squarefree set through an enormous finite dyadic boundary is a motivated nontrivial cutoff extending the older OEIS n<=20737 observation. A future researcher investigating final squarefree terms or mixed-base digit obstructions could use this exact finite negative result, even though the boundary 16384 is computationally selected and it does not settle the global problem. This significance is the mathematical obstruction/census, not code correctness or novelty alone.
